clue.text: Group of officers, heads of naval detachments

parts.note: the punctuation mark printed in the clue itself is a comma

indicators.note: heads of means the first letter of each of the two following words is taken

explanation.surface: A naval officer cadre is being put together from the leaders of various detachments.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma printed after 'officers' is itself a piece of wordplay, supplying COMMA; the initials of 'naval detachments' add ND.
explanation.definitionFit: A command is a body of troops or officers under one commander, so it is a group of officers.

clue.text: Struggle to disentangle 16 down

parts.note: to comb hair is to disentangle it
the answer at 16 down is the element astatine, whose chemical symbol is At

explanation.surface: Someone is struggling to work out a tangled cross-reference in the puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: Combat is fighting, a struggle between opposing forces.

clue.text: Relating to fast, tailless fictional bloodhound

indicators.note: tailless means the last letter of the detective's name is docked

parts.note: Maigret is Georges Simenon's fictional detective, a bloodhound in the slang sense of a sleuth

explanation.surface: A fictional dog has lost its tail and needs to go without food.
explanation.definitionFit: Maigre describes a day of abstinence from meat in the Catholic calendar, so it relates to fasting.

clue.text: Ace tenant merrily taking possession of duke's house

indicators.note: taking possession of means the rearranged letters hold the next piece within them
merrily suggests letters cavorting about, so these words are rearranged

parts.note: D is the standard abbreviation for duke

explanation.surface: A cheerful tenant of high standing moves into a ducal mansion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'merrily' turns ACE TENANT into ATTENANCE, and 'taking possession of' puts D inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: In theatre a house is the audience present, which is the attendance at a performance.

clue.text: On reflection micron's a tiny amount, in fact

indicators.note: on reflection means the pieces are seen as in a mirror, read backwards

parts.note: the Greek letter mu is the symbol for micron
a tad is a tiny amount

explanation.surface: Thinking it over, a micron really is a minuscule quantity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On reflection' turns MUTAD into the answer as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: A datum is a single piece of information, a known fact used as a basis.

clue.text: Old Scotsman's colourful project

indicators.note: the 's stands for has, so the old Scotsman has the next piece inside him

parts.note: the Picts were an ancient people of northern Scotland
red is a colour, hence colourful

explanation.surface: An ancient Scot is putting on a vivid painted project.
explanation.definitionFit: To project is to forecast or estimate the future, which is to predict it.

clue.text: Bouncer quietly getting Oscar to leave club

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to go is to leave
a club is a heavy stick

explanation.surface: A nightclub doorman quietly persuades a man named Oscar to leave the premises.
explanation.definitionFit: A pogo stick is a spring-loaded toy that bounces its rider up and down, so a bouncer.

clue.text: Destroys country house, top to bottom

indicators.note: top to bottom means the first letter of this down entry is moved to its foot

parts.note: a seat is a large country house

explanation.surface: Someone is wrecking a stately home from the attic to the cellar.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that eats away at a thing corrodes and so destroys it.

clue.text: Admirer's agreement to marry — but not yet

parts.note: I do is the words spoken to agree to marriage at a wedding
later means at some future time, not yet

explanation.surface: A suitor has had a proposal accepted, but the wedding is put off.
explanation.definitionFit: An idolater worships idols, hence any devoted admirer of someone.

clue.text: Wrongly enter hairdressing establishment offering health treatments

indicators.note: dressing means the hair is wrapped around the next piece, as dressing covers something

parts.note: tresses are long locks of hair
a spa is a resort offering health treatments

explanation.surface: Someone barges uninvited into a salon that also does spa treatments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hairdressing' must be split: 'hair' gives TRESS and 'dressing' puts SPA inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To trespass is to go onto land or premises without the right to do so.

clue.text: Nice way of saying Arachne's somewhat vacuous and a bit wet

parts.note: in Nice, a French city, the setter referring to herself would say moi, French for me

indicators.note: vacuous means emptied, so only the outer letters of the word remain

explanation.surface: The setter coyly admits to being a little empty-headed and slightly damp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' is the French city, not the adjective, so the setter's 'me' becomes MOI; 'vacuous' empties 'somewhat' to ST.
explanation.definitionFit: Moist means slightly wet, damp rather than soaked.

clue.text: It might drop me, if uninitiated in its use

definitions.text: It might drop me, if uninitiated in its use

indicators.note: uninitiated means each of the four words loses its initial letter

explanation.surface: A nervous novice fears a high wire might send them falling.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the first letter of 'It', 'might', 'drop' and 'me' leaves T, IGHT, ROP, E; the whole clue then describes the rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A tightrope walker who is inexperienced may well be dropped by the wire.

clue.text: Expert on land usage cultivating margins, too

indicators.note: cultivating means working the soil over, so these letters are turned over and rearranged

explanation.surface: A land-use specialist is farming the field edges as well.
explanation.definitionFit: An agronomist studies soil management and crop production, so is an expert in land use.

clue.text: Privileged American used to be attracted to power

parts.note: was is the past tense of be, so used to be
P is the physics abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: A rich American was once drawn towards political power.
explanation.definitionFit: A WASP is a White Anglo-Saxon Protestant, a member of the traditionally privileged US elite.

clue.text: Interest as founder returns to old place

indicators.note: to founder is to collapse, so these letters fall apart and are rebuilt

explanation.surface: A company founder takes back an interest in the old firm.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinstate something is to restore it to its former position.

clue.text: Of sound mind, ultimately buffered by stout optimism

indicators.note: ultimately buffered by means the final letter of the first piece is cushioned inside the following one

parts.note: someone of sound mind is sane
Guinness is the famous Irish stout

explanation.surface: Someone stays sane and cheerful with the help of a pint of stout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately buffered by' moves the E at the end of SANE into the middle of GUINNESS, between its two Ns.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanguineness is a cheerful, confident disposition, the quality of being hopeful.

clue.text: Freedom fighters beleaguer ill-assorted internees

indicators.note: internees are people held within, so the answer is held inside these words

explanation.surface: Rebels besiege a motley group of camp prisoners.
explanation.definitionFit: Guerillas fight irregular wars, often presenting themselves as freedom fighters.

clue.text: Radioactive element, which is used to lower cholesterol in casualty

indicators.note: in means the drug is placed inside the hospital department

parts.note: A and E (accident and emergency) is the British hospital casualty department

parts.words: which is used to lower cholesterol
parts.note: a statin is a drug prescribed to lower cholesterol

explanation.surface: Doctors in the emergency room use a radioactive substance to cut cholesterol.
explanation.definitionFit: Astatine is a rare radioactive chemical element, number 85.

clue.text: Disturbed Harry Lime's last day

parts.note: to harry someone is to harass or molest them

indicators.note: last means the final letter of the name is taken

explanation.surface: The final day of Harry Lime, villain of The Third Man, is recalled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry Lime' looks like the Third Man character, but 'Harry' is a verb meaning harass.
explanation.definitionFit: Molested means pestered or troubled, so disturbed.

clue.text: Inspecting, unannounced, what teenagers get up to in bathroom?

definitions.meaning: carrying out a random inspection without warning

definitions.text: what teenagers get up to in bathroom?
definitions.meaning: teenagers examining their faces in the mirror for pimples

explanation.definitionFit: Spot-checking is making a random inspection without notice; a spotty teenager literally checks spots.

clue.text: Copper said goodbye

indicators.note: said means the two letters are spoken as they sound

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A police officer bid farewell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman, but it is the element, symbol Cu, whose letters spoken give the farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: See you is an informal farewell, short for see you later.

clue.text: Where French children learn to core fruit

indicators.note: to core means to remove the central letter of the fruit

parts.note: the lychee is a sweet Asian fruit

explanation.surface: French schoolchildren are being taught to core fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Lycées are French secondary schools.

clue.text: Top copy with illiterate's signature

parts.note: to ape is to copy
a person unable to write signs with a cross, X

explanation.surface: A duplicate of a top document is signed with a cross by someone who cannot write.
explanation.definitionFit: The apex is the highest point or peak.

clue.text: Sardonically mentioning carefree fellow

indicators.note: mentioning means the name is spoken aloud

parts.note: living the life of Riley means living carefree, so Riley is a carefree fellow

explanation.surface: Someone talks sarcastically about an easy-going chap.
explanation.definitionFit: Wryly means with dry, mocking humour, so sardonically.

clue.text: Perhaps the elder Turgenev gets noticed periodically?

indicators.note: periodically means taking letters at regular intervals, every other one

explanation.surface: Was the older Turgenev occasionally recognised?
explanation.walkthrough: 'the elder' looks like a senior relative, but it is the elder bush.
explanation.definitionFit: The elder is a species of shrub or small tree, so an example of a tree.

clue.text: Party line developed into mutual exchange

indicators.note: developed means these letters evolve into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: The party line has turned into a two-way dialogue.
explanation.definitionFit: Interplay is the reciprocal action between things, a mutual exchange.

clue.text: State occasion making a mint

indicators.note: to state is to say, so the word is spoken aloud

parts.note: an occasion is a time when something happens

explanation.surface: A grand state ceremony is making a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State occasion' looks like a ceremony, but 'State' means say; 'mint' is the plant family, not a fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: Thyme belongs to the mint family of herbs, Lamiaceae.

clue.text: This team makes you tea

parts.note: the word 'team' without its final letter becomes 'tea'

explanation.surface: A team brews tea for you.
explanation.definitionFit: With no end, the word for a group of players turns into a hot drink.

clue.text: Qualified agreements to rework endless subsystem

indicators.note: to rework means the remaining letters are reshaped
endless means the word loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: An engineer agrees to redesign an infinite part of the system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' strips 'subsystem' to UBSYSTE, which 'to rework' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Yes-buts are replies that agree with reservations, qualified agreements.
